result: The authors designed corrective lenses for long GRIN rods (6.4 mm and 8.8 mm) using optical simulations. Simulations predicted that corrective lenses would increase the diffraction-limited FOV radius by 3.50× and 3.35× for the two probe lengths, respectively, and improve PSF quality across the FOV.
evaluation: All reviewers affirm the simulation work. Reviewer 1 states 'the design, characterization, and simulations are clear and thorough,' and Reviewer 3 notes 'numerous experiments and simulations are presented to evaluate the performance.' No concerns are raised about the simulation methodology or predictions.

result: The authors fabricated corrective lenses using 3D microprinting based on 2P lithography to create prototypes, then replicated them using a molding procedure for efficient production.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'the lenses are made by a molding process that appears practical and easy to adopt,' indicating acceptance of the fabrication approach. Reviewer 1 also mentions that the authors 'addressed issues I raised in initial review, including...descriptions of manufacturing and assembly yield,' suggesting initial concerns were resolved.

result: Experimental characterization using fluorescent films showed that corrected microendoscopes collected fluorescence signal over longer distances from the FOV center with more homogeneous FWHM values. The effective FOV radius increased by 2.17× and 1.53× for the 6.4 mm and 8.8 mm probes, corresponding to FOV area enlargements of 4.7× and 2.3×.
evaluation: The editor states the authors 'provide convincing evidence showing that the obtained field of view is significantly increased with corrected, versus uncorrected microendoscopes.' Reviewer 3 highlights 'PSFs measured with corrected microendoscopes 75µm from the centre of the FOV show a significant reduction in optical aberrations' as convincing evidence.

result: Imaging of fixed brain slices demonstrated that aberration correction enabled clear resolution of neuronal somata and processes in lateral FOV portions, whereas uncorrected lenses produced dim, aberrated, and hardly detectable structures in peripheral regions.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly states 'Morphological imaging of fixed brain slices shows that optical resolution is maintained over a larger field of view with corrected microendoscopes compared to uncorrected ones, allowing neuronal processes to be revealed even close to the edge of the FOV' as convincing evidence.

result: Using synthetic calcium data simulating the mouse olfactory cortex, the authors showed that corrected microendoscopes enabled detection of more ROIs with higher SNR, increased the maximal radial distance for high-SNR ROIs, reduced cross-contamination between adjacent neurons, maintained higher purity of source demixing across radial distance, and improved correlation with ground truth signals.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'simulations are used to motivate the benefits of extended field of view, demonstrating that more cells can be recorded, with less mixing of signals in extracted traces.' Reviewer 3 states 'Using synthetic calcium data, the authors showed that the signals obtained with the corrected microendoscopes have a significantly stronger correlation with the ground truth signals than those obtained with uncorrected microendoscopes' as convincing evidence.

result: In vivo imaging in the mouse olfactory cortex using 8.8 mm corrected microendoscopes showed that peak SNR of calcium events was constant across the FOV, pairwise correlation of adjacent neurons did not depend on radial distance, and correlation between neuron pairs decreased with their reciprocal distance, demonstrating unbiased sampling of neural population activity.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 states the authors 'were able to make measurements from large numbers of cells simultaneously in vivo in a difficult preparation' and that they 'achieved their aims, as evidenced by the images presented.' Reviewer 1 also notes the authors 'did a good job of addressing issues I raised in initial review, including...basic analysis of the in vivo recordings relative to odor presentations.'

result: Experimental measurements of optical performance were generally in good agreement with simulation predictions, though simulated PSF sizes tended to be smaller than experimentally measured PSFs, possibly due to differences between excitation and emission PSFs, consideration of only first-order aberrations in simulations, and experimental variability.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes the authors 'did a good job of addressing issues I raised in initial review, including...explanations in the text of differences between ex vivo and in vivo imaging conditions,' suggesting initial concerns about discrepancies were adequately addressed. No reviewer challenges the comparison or the authors' explanations.

result: Long corrected microendoscopes (6.4 mm and 8.8 mm length, 500 µm diameter) provide improved spatial resolution enabling imaging in significantly enlarged FOVs, representing powerful new tools for population imaging with unprecedented large FOV and high spatial resolution in the most ventral regions of the mouse brain with minimal invasiveness.
evaluation: The editor describes this as a 'valuable study' presenting a 'potentially key method' and states the approach 'can be readily adopted by neuroscientists who wish to image neuronal activity deep in the brain.' Reviewer 2 notes 'the experiments convincingly demonstrate the advantages of the corrective lenses' and that 'the implementation of these long corrected micro-endoscopes...will also enable deep imaging in larger mammals.'

result: The corrected microendoscopes are ready-to-use, requiring no modification of microscope hardware or software, do not limit temporal resolution, and can be coupled with standard 2P microscopes or portable microscopes for freely moving animals.
evaluation: The editor emphasizes 'the approach described in this paper does not require any microscope or software modifications.' Reviewer 2 states 'the main strength of this method is that it does not require hardware or software modifications, nor does it limit the system's temporal resolution.' Reviewer 3 notes 'the solution presented in this paper does not require any modification of the optical microscope.'

result: GRIN lenses have intrinsic optical aberrations that severely degrade imaging performance by decreasing SNR and spatial resolution, especially in lateral FOV portions, leading to restricted FOV and fewer recorded neurons. These effects are particularly relevant for long GRIN lenses needed to reach deep brain regions.
evaluation: These are background claims establishing the problem being addressed. Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'the authors present an approach to correct GRIN lens aberrations, which primarily cause a decrease in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), particularly in the lateral regions of the field-of-view (FOV), thereby limiting the usable FOV.' No reviewer questions these foundational claims.

result: Previous work by the same group demonstrated aberration correction for GRIN lenses <4.1 mm using 3D microprinting, but these were too short to reach the most ventral mouse brain regions, and applicability to longer GRIN lenses with stronger aberrations remained to be proven.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes 'this paper closely follows the thread of earlier work from the same group (esp. Antonini et al, 2020; eLife), filling out the quiver of available extended-field-of-view 2P endoscopes with these longer lenses.' Reviewer 2 states 'this approach was previously demonstrated by the same lab for GRIN lenses shorter than 4.1 mm...In the current work, the authors extend their method to a new class of GRIN lenses with lengths exceeding 6 mm.'
